sentences.text: Unknown vs Aggrieved By The Decree And Order Passed ... on

18 July, 2023
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice V.Gopala Krishna Rao
 M.A.C.M.A.No. 2432 of 2015
Judgement:
Aggrieved by the decree and order passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims
Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Nellore, in M.V.O.P.No.424 of 2012, whereby the petition
filed by the petitioner under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of
Rs.5,00,000/- for the death of her husband in a motor vehicle accident that took place on
21.02.2010 was allowed in part awarding compensation of Rs.2,79,000/-, this instant appeal is
preferred by the respondent.

2. For the sake of convenience, both the parties in the appeal will be referred to as they are arrayed
in the claim petition.

3. The brief averments in the petition filed by the petitioner are as follows:
Vgkr,J Macma No.2432 of 2015 On 21.02.2010 at about 7.00 a.m. the deceased
was returning to his house from Pamulavaripalem village of Indukurpet on his
bicycle and when he reached near the house of Pamula Chandraiah, a tractor bearing
registration No.AP 26D 8901 being driven by its driver in a rash and negligent
manner came in opposite direction and dashed against the deceased, as a result, the
deceased sustained grievous injuries and later succumbed to injuries on the way to
the hospital.

The respondent being the owner of the offending tractor is liable to pay
the compensation to the petitioner.

4. The respondent field a counter by denying the manner of accident, age, occupation and income of
the deceased.

It is pleaded that the accident occurred due to negligence of the deceased, there was
no rashness or negligence on the part of the driver of the tractor, therefore, the respondent is not
liable to pay any compensation to the petitioner.

Vgkr,J
5.
Based on the above pleadings of both the parties, the following issues were settled for trial by the
Tribunal:

1) Whether the accident took place due to the rash and negligent driving of the tractor
bearing registration No.AP 26D 8901 and whether the deceased had also contributed
in taking place of the accident?

1

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
3) To what relief?
6.

During the course of enquiry in the claim petition, on behalf of the petitioner, P.Ws.1 and 2 were
examined and Exs.A.1 to A.5 were marked.

On behalf of the respondent, R.W.1 was examined, but
no documentary evidence was adduced.

7. At the culmination of the enquiry, based on the material available on record, the Tribunal came to
the conclusion that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the
offending tractor and accordingly, allowed the petition in part awarding compensation of
Rs.2,79,000/-.

Questioning the legal Vgkr,J validity of the said order, the appellant/respondent
preferred the present appeal.

8. Heard learned counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
9.

Learned counsel for the appellant/respondent would submit that the compensation awarded is
excessive and the rate of interest awarded by the Tribunal @ 7.5% p.a. is also exorbitant.

10. Now, the point for determination is:
Whether the order of the Tribunal needs any interference of this Court?

11. Point: It is the case of the petitioner that the deceased was returning to his house from
Pamulavaripalem village of Indukurpet on his bicycle and when he reached near the house of
Pamula Chandraiah, a tractor bearing registration No.AP 26D 8901 being driven by its driver in a
rash and negligent manner came in opposite direction and dashed against the deceased resulting in
the Vgkr,J accident and the deceased sustained injuries and while he was being shifted to the
Government Hospital, Nellore in 108 ambulance, he succumbed to injuries on the way.

In order to
establish her case, the petitioner got examined herself as P.W.1 and another witness as P.W.2.

P.W.1
is none other than the wife of the deceased and she is not an eye witness to the accident.

P.W.2 is an
eye witness to the accident.

The petitioner also relied on Ex.A.1-attested copy of first information
report, Ex.A.4-certified copy of M.V.I. report and Ex.A.5- certified copy of charge sheet.

Ex.A.1 goes
to show that a case was registered against the driver of the offending tractor.

Ex .A.4 discloses that
the accident occurred not due to any mechanical defects in the offending tractor.
Ex. A.5

reveals that
after due investigation, the police filed a charge sheet against the driver of the offending tractor.

The
evidence of P.W.2 coupled with Exs.A.1, A.4 and A.5 clearly proves about the rash and negligent
driving of the driver of the offending tractor resulting in the accident.

On appreciation of the
evidence on record, the Tribunal also came to Vgkr,J the same conclusion.

Therefore, I do not find
any legal flaw or infirmity in the said finding g
iven by the Tribunal.
12. Coming to the compensation, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,79,000/- towards compensation.
The material on record reveals that the deceased was aged about 45 years at the time of accident.

The contention of the petitioner is that the deceased was doing business in cattle and Unknown vs Aggrieved By The Decree And Order Passed ... on 18 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/165463476/
2 used to earn Rs.10,000/- per month.
But, in order to prove the earnings of the deceased, no positive evidence was produced by the petitioner before the Tribunal.
However, by giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal arrived the monthly income of the deceased at Rs.2,000/- p.m. i.e., Rs.24,000/- per annum.
The petitioner is the sole dependent on the deceased.

Therefore, after deducting 1/3 from out of annual income towards personal living expenses of the deceased and by applying the appropriate multiplier '14' to the age group of the deceased as per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Varma case, the Tribunal arrived the loss of dependency at Rs.2,24,000/-
VGKR,J (Rs.16,000/- (Rs.24,000/- - Rs.8,000/-) x multiplier '14').
The Tribunal also awarded an amount of Rs.30,000/- towards loss of consortium to the petitioner, Rs.20,000/- towards funeral expenses of the deceased and Rs.5,000/- towards transport expenses.
In total, by giving cogent reasons, the Tribunal awarded an amount of Rs.2,79,000/- towards compensation to the petitioner.
Therefore, I do not find any illegality or irregularity in the said finding given by the Tribunal.

13. Insofar as awarding of interest @ 7.5% p.a. is concerned, this Court finds merit in the submission of the learned standing counsel for the appellant/Insurance company that the Tribunal awarded exorbitant rate of interest, since the accident occurred in the year 2010, therefore, the same has to be reduced from 7.5% p.a. to 6% p.a.
14.

Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of and the decree and order dated 10.04.2015 passed by the Chairman, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal-cum-Principal District Judge, Nellore, in VGKR,J M.V.O.P.No.424 of 2012 is modified by reducing the rate of interest from 7.5% p.a. to 6% p.a.
